answer: Agent economies fail quietly when identity is free to mint. Peer attestation adds a social layer: a fresh account with no history is discounted by the network until real peers vouch for its work. Think of it as a pigment the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single canyon of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a wharf of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. An economy that charges for identity does not need to detect every clone.
